authority_basis.scalar_role: non-secret opaque local lookup, correlation and uniqueness handle
authority_basis.opaque_meaning: Consumers compare exact bytes; decoding a counter or predicting the next value grants no permission.
required_conjunction: exact expected owner/relation object type, and exact built-in scalar types; reject wrappers and subclasses
exact original retained process-local object, not a reconstructed equal object
owner-specific original registry entry and retained upstream graph
issuing PID and current original process incarnation with independent process-local owner secret
constant-time valid domain/role-separated HMAC over exact originally retained canonical bindings
matching immutable stable fingerprint where required, separately from current state authenticity
current generations, observation, admission, local fence, eligibility and permanent one-shot/tombstone checks
authority_basis.wire_rule: JSON scalars may correlate an already authenticated retained exchange. Neither a wire ID nor JSON reconstruction creates a registry entry or original object. A controller must obtain separately authenticated admission through its future authenticated original channel; the scalar admission ID alone never suffices.
authority_basis.trust_boundary_rule: No scoped scalar crosses a boundary as a bearer capability under the frozen contracts. If an implementation accepts ID-only lookup as permission, this encoding is inapplicable: stop unresolved and require a separately reviewed capability/authentication contract before effects. Making the handle longer does not repair an ID-only authority path.
authority_basis.threat_model_limit: A malicious caller may know or guess all IDs and supply copied values/objects. Arbitrary execution that can mutate private registries, steal secrets or bypass validators is outside the owner abstraction; handles do not provide memory isolation.

encoding.alphabet: prefix from wcxatrod followed only by 0123456789abcdef
encoding.canonical_case: lowercase only; reject uppercase rather than normalize
encoding.serialization: exact built-in str, ASCII, one canonical JSON string under the frozen encoding; no padding changes, escapes, whitespace, signs, separators or alternate spellings
encoding.generation_method: Owner-reserved positive monotonic integer, represented as exactly sixteen lowercase zero-padded hexadecimal digits following the field-family prefix. This is a specification only; no generator is supplied.
encoding.capacity_rationale: All classes independently retain histories across an otherwise unbounded process-incarnation lifetime; no audited class has a smaller universal count bound. This phase chooses a 63-bit nonwrapping allocation capacity consistent with C:/framing/primitive_rules/positive_int; that historical rule constrains message sequences, not the existing generic ID strings, and does not mandate this choice. This is a bounded availability policy, not a cryptographic minimum. Equal widths reflect the independently shared retention/capacity obligation, not a demand that semantic classes match or a byte-fit objective. Both 32-bit and 63-bit handles can be security-correct with explicit exhaustion; a smaller bound has no independent class-specific evidence here. Full SHA256 would add authentication responsibilities these scalars do not have.
encoding.additive_grammar: These predicates constrain future values of existing generic id fields only; S:/definitions/id remains unchanged. Prefix, suffix range and exact field domain must all validate. No issued historical ID is re-encoded.

generation_semantics.namespace: One retained allocation namespace per future issuer process incarnation, shared across every instance of the participating future owner domains; never one resetting counter per owner object.
generation_semantics.reservation: A single abstract monotonic reservation ledger assigns a fresh integer across all participating families and owners. Family prefix selects semantic domain; exact owner module/phase/schema/role and original relation are additionally authenticated. Independent owner instances may not start their own overlapping namespace.
generation_semantics.thread_safety: Reservation, increment and issued/tombstoned collision check are one linearizable critical section. No assumption about the GIL. Owner registration may follow, but any reserved value stays burned on failure, exception or cancellation.
generation_semantics.collision_handling: At reservation, reject any existing reserved, active, terminal or tombstoned key before claiming it. Registration may publish only that issuer's own newly created reservation, once; reject a foreign reservation or an already published/terminal/tombstoned ID. An unexpected collision or missing namespace continuity is an invariant failure: no overwrite, no retry with the same value, no alias, no dispatch; invalidate affected eligibility and retain burned values.
generation_semantics.wrap: Never wrap, truncate, modulo, saturate or restart; reject allocation before exceeding 9223372036854775807. Exhaustion withdraws new issuance, not cleanup of retained originals.
generation_semantics.fork_boundary: PID mismatch invalidates all inherited originals and allocator state before validation or issuance. A forked child may not continue an inherited namespace or lock; it needs a new empty process-incarnation namespace and independently initialized owner secrets through a future reviewed initialization path. No such path is implemented here.
generation_semantics.restart_boundary: A fresh process incarnation may repeat printable strings only in a disjoint new namespace with new secrets and empty original-object registry. Old objects, JSON and HMACs cannot be imported or reattached. PID equality alone never permits continuity, including after PID reuse.
generation_semantics.reload_boundary: Module reload, registry recreation, allocator replacement or secret rotation cannot reset counters while any namespace originals/tombstones can be recognized. Retain namespace continuity or fail closed for new issuance and old eligibility. No rehydration from serialized IDs.
generation_semantics.lifetime: Reservation histories and permanent terminal tombstones last to process-incarnation termination, independently of whether the original operational object remains live. Strong originals/graph remain as required by their owning contracts.
generation_semantics.terminal: Terminal records may authenticate historical evidence but cannot restore readiness. Never remove a tombstone to free a scalar; no namespace recycling after registry cleanup.
generation_semantics.domain_separation: Prefix validation rejects class substitution before lookup. A prefix is not an HMAC domain: independent existing owner secret/domain/role separation and exact original graph comparisons remain mandatory for cross-owner substitution within the same class.
generation_semantics.allocation_is_not_coordination: The abstract reservation ledger concerns name uniqueness only. It does not hold existing private owner locks, bridge owner stores, authenticate an admission, spend a facet or establish a cross-owner effect transaction. Concrete synchronization remains a future implementation obligation.
generation_semantics.caller_control: Only the authenticated issuing owner reserves a new value; callers may echo an already bound value but cannot select, register, overwrite or alias it. Parse/equality checks use exact strings without coercion.
generation_semantics.random_alternatives: No scoped scalar requires unpredictability. Random or cryptographic random allocation is not the accepted primitive for these future fields; the frozen historical random conventions remain untouched. Observation challenges and independent HMAC secrets retain their stronger existing requirements.
